result.question: Transformer 1 at site MAIN seems to show co rising alongside thermal gases, and I want the right follow-up work on the books without creating duplicates. First, compare co, ethylene and methane at the first and last oil samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, and run a fault classification on the last sample to confirm whether the fault is thermal with paper involved. Then check all open and pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1. If none of them already covers an oil sample retest or an insulation check, create one corrective work order that covers both. Give it priority 2 if the classification comes back T2/T3 with paper involved, and priority 3 otherwise. Code it with the failure code from our catalog that best matches the fault. Assign it to the technician who has the fewest open work orders at MAIN, choosing among the technicians who have worked on Transformer 1 before. Pick a start date within the next 7 days that doesn't land on a day that already has 3 or more scheduled work orders at MAIN. If a matching open work order already exists, don't create a new one. Instead, show me its number, priority and assigned technician, and recommend whether its priority should be raised given the classification. If co is null in either sample, say that paper involvement can't be confirmed and make the work order an oil retest only.
result.answer:
The work-order backend is rejecting writes outright (403 Forbidden on both the counter and a direct document write), so the work order could not be created. The analysis is complete; here is the result and the exact work order that's ready to submit once write access is restored.

## 1. Oil sample comparison (Transformer 1, 2024‑01‑15 → 2024‑01‑18)

| Gas | First sample (01‑15) | Last sample (01‑18) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| CO | 32 ppm | 33 ppm | +1 ppm (+3%, effectively flat) |
| Ethylene (C₂H₄) | 16 684 ppm | 16 600 ppm | −84 ppm |
| Methane (CH₄) | 7 406 ppm | 7 350 ppm | −56 ppm |

CO is non‑null in both samples, so paper involvement can be assessed. Note that CO is **not** actually rising in this window — it is flat and very low (32–35 ppm), while the thermal gases are high but stable.

## 2. Fault classification (last sample)

The `interpret_dga` tool returned "LLM unavailable" twice, so this is a manual IEC 60599 Rogers‑ratio interpretation:

- C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = 7/16600 ≈ 0.0004 (< 0.1)
- CH₄/H₂ = 7350/2900 ≈ 2.53 (> 1)
- C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = 16600/5450 ≈ 3.05 (1–4)

→ **T2 thermal fault (300–700 °C)** — consistent with the note already on WO 1000051.
**Paper involvement: not confirmed.** CO is only 33 ppm (well below typical concern levels) and CO₂/CO ≈ 40 — a pattern pointing to oil oxidation/atmospheric CO₂ rather than hot cellulose. Under your rule this is **priority 3**, with a recommendation to raise to 2 if the retest shows CO trending up or furans elevated.

## 3. Existing work orders on Transformer 1

- Open (WAPPR): **1000051** — "OLTC inspection … suspected contact wear/coking", priority 1, no technician assigned, no failure code.
- Pending approval (APPR): none.

1000051 covers the tap changer only — **no existing WO covers an oil retest or insulation check**, so a new one is warranted (no duplicate).

## 4. Work order to create (blocked by 403)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Asset / site | Transformer 1 / MAIN |
| Type / priority | CM / **3** |
| Description | DGA oil sample retest and winding insulation check (T2 thermal fault, paper involvement unconfirmed) |
| Failure code | **FC006** – overheating or high temperature reading (closest catalog match to a thermal fault) |
| Target start | **2026‑10‑01** — the MAIN calendar shows 0 scheduled WOs for 2026‑09‑30 → 10‑07, so any day qualifies |
| Technician | **Unresolved** — see below |

**Technician constraint can't be satisfied as written:** no work order on Transformer 1 (open or historical) has ever had labor assigned, so the pool of "technicians who have worked on Transformer 1" is empty. Site‑wide, MECHTECH2 (MECH) and HVACTECH1 (HVAC) each have exactly 1 open WO — a tie, and neither is an electrical craft. I did not want to guess here; tell me which to use (or give me an electrical labor code) and I'll assign with a 2026‑10‑01 start.

## What I need from you

1. Restore write access to the work‑order database (the CouchDB endpoint at 127.0.0.1:58135 is returning 403 for creates), then I'll re‑submit the WO above unchanged.
2. Confirm the technician choice for the assignment.

Also worth flagging: the premise that CO is rising isn't supported by the 01‑15 → 01‑18 data. If you saw the rise in a different window, tell me the dates and I'll re‑run the comparison.
